checks: The given positive mixture equals dm/(ML) as a measure. Thus every positive row is absolutely continuous with respect to the sampled d-volume and carried by the sampled union, as required by the accepted row lemma. The full barycenter, L-mean and tilted marginal have exactly its normalization.

Every active source plane contacts its row. The row lemma assigns each row one slope, and the only row of a particular slope supplies the whole restricted tilted marginal for that label. Positivity of L makes its null sets agree with the original mixed-volume null sets.

Conversely on an active-plane contact cell, at a fiber-interior differentiability point the continuous slope of the affine majorant equals the derivative of L. Fiber boundaries and unequal-slope affine ties are null on each full-dimensional sampled fiber. Both inclusion directions therefore give equality of the original volume restrictions separately at every site.

The contact cell is compact convex as an intersection of affine inequalities with C. The hull of all its sampled sections is contained in the cell and retains those same sections at each sampled base, including lower-dimensional sections. The original complete P excludes extra integer sites. Positive sections contain balls, so any anchored integer combination of them again has positive volume and the positive support is a closed minor.

The added buffered hypotheses exactly invoke the accepted source-gradient closure and disjoint parities at all qualifying maximizing bases, including zero-weight ones. Every occurring target label has a source by the row lemma. In inherited rank one a label with two distinct source sites fills their integer interval, hence includes two successive inherited lattice sites and both parities. This precludes another label, while otherwise two labels each have one source.

Rank zero has at most one distinct source base. A sole label has all sampled d-volume and the original canonical hull represents it. For two labels the closed representatives may meet in null boundaries, which is consistent with equality of volume restrictions. The sources 50a9575831060dc5 §§2–3 make this same distinction and do not imply a class depth payment.

dependencies.hypotheses: Apply with the stated sampled union, finite affine L>0, positive weights, full row barycenters and exact L-means. The positive marginal identity forces support on the sampled union and gives its label occurrence, unique continuous slope, and contact-cell assertions.

Use the same complete base, canonical actual fibers, concave positive-on-interiors F, L^sF^(1−s), the same nonvertical shifted thresholds and pure-base rule, and all the assumed unique own-interior proper attaining maximizing marks. The inherited classes of these marks are closed and parity-separated.

overlap.comparison: It obtains gradient-preserving row transport from an additional buffered separator and gives exact tilted and unweighted label balances. It does not identify a unique-source label with one contact body or prove compatible representatives by the rank-one parity argument.

It proves lattice closure and disjoint inherited parities for proper deepest source classes. Those facts are used here to control the number of rows per label and to obtain compatible target representatives, a separate conclusion.

readability: The representative is an equality of d-volume restrictions in each fiber. The closed contact sections themselves need not partition as sets.
review_method: Independent cold proof read on the frozen candidate, followed by original-scope and exact dependency comparison, with exact rational checks where applicable.
summary: A unique row for a label gives a convex representative fiber by fiber. The rank-one reduction correctly uses closure and parity of all eligible deepest bases, rather than only the weighted sources.
